title: Camera: what to do, when, in any engine (learned from 27 viral references + cinema.js)

entries.when: hook: the first 0.5-1.5 s, the claim or the stake is spoken
entries.do: Start already close (medium-close or close) on the subject and add a fast 6-10 % push or punch-in that finishes inside 1.2 s; one idea only; the first caption word lands on frame 0-6.

evidence.note: face cam opens on a title card then pushes; handheld+dutch share 0.39
opens on a smiling close-up, a hook sentence about the stake
opens on two faces, then a hard cut to an extreme close-up at 4 s

anti_patterns: a wide establishing shot as the first frame
greeting or logo before the claim
a static first 3 s

how_by_engine.2d-flat: scale the layer about the subject centre with a whip-ease; add 2-3 px blur at the start of the move
how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: dolly the camera 6-10 % toward the actor; keep the horizon level
how_by_engine.3d: dolly-in plus 2-4 degree tilt-up; lens 35 mm equivalent
how_by_engine.face-cam: crop-in 6-10 % on the face, cut to the overlay card at the first noun
how_by_engine.board: zoom the first element from 85 to 100 % with a pop; the headline lands with it

entries.when: establishing a place or situation after the hook (story styles), 4-9 s
entries.do: Wide or very wide, high or eye-level, slow drone orbit or crane-down that reveals the object of the story (the tree, the coaster loop, the haystack); one clear subject in the third; hold at least 3 s because it carries narration.

evidence.note: wide road + tree, drone drift, speed-limit sign as part of the world
establishing shots up to 18 s with a slow push on the coaster
haystack seen from below then wide town

anti_patterns: orbit faster than the sentence
two establishing shots in a row

how_by_engine.2d-flat: slow parallax pan across 3-4 layers (sky, far, mid, near) 5-8 % travel
how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: orbit 15-40 degrees around the actor and prop
how_by_engine.3d: crane-down from high wide to eye-level

entries.when: a reveal: a number, a twist, an object appears, 'and then'
entries.do: Whip pan or snap zoom (0.2-0.35 s, motion blur on), land on the revealed thing, hold 1.0-1.5 s unmoving so it can be read; a whoosh starts 40 ms before the landing and an impact sits on the landing frame.

evidence.note: snap to the upside-down cart then a hard hold
cut to a spotlit host with a golden halo on the reveal line
counter badge appears, camera drops to the chest

anti_patterns: reveal and next move in the same second
whip without sound

how_by_engine.2d-flat: horizontal slide-blur transition plus scale 105 to 100
how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: whip pan to the prop, then lock
how_by_engine.3d: whip pan 60-90 degrees plus focus pull
how_by_engine.face-cam: hard cut to the overlay card; card scales 92 to 100 %
how_by_engine.board: the new element springs in 85 to 100 % and the rest dims 30 %

entries.when: a character reacts: fear, doubt, anger, shock, a thought turns
entries.do: Extreme close-up on eyes and brows (or the whole face filling 70 %); 0.9-1.6 s; a slow 3-5 % push, one blink or eye-dart inside the shot; cut back to the two-shot when the line ends.

evidence.note: sweating cap-boy close-up at 27 s, glasses face at 4 s
red-lit glasses close-up on the news beat, phone face close-up
tight push on the near face at the payoff line

anti_patterns: close-up with a neutral face
more than 3 close-ups in 10 s

how_by_engine.2d-flat: scale the face layer to 170-220 %, swap to the emotion mouth/brow set
how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: switch to the sprite's close sprite or dolly to 0.5 m
how_by_engine.3d: 85 mm close-up, shallow depth of field

entries.when: a character or host explains a point for 2-5 s
entries.do: Medium shot, eye-level, slow 3-5 % push over the sentence; the hand gesture lands on the keyword; cut on the sentence end, not mid-word.

evidence.note: host bust stays fixed while the panel changes; host pose changes on emphasis
same host, 7 poses over 65 s
character foreground, slow push, cards float in front

anti_patterns: same pose for more than 4 s
push that reverses

how_by_engine.board: panel holds; the host pose changes

entries.when: listing items, steps, plugins, repos (tutorial styles)
entries.do: Do not cut. One continuous infographic shot per item; inside it a new element enters every 1.5-2.2 s (title, then proof, then number); the item number is on screen all the time; on the next item the whole board morphs (cards slide out), not a hard cut.

evidence.note: 1 cut in 10 s on a white grid, numbered step chips, big numerals
dial 0 to 10x, device list, 1 to 23 fixes: all inside one shot
3D tilted card arrays and a ledger bar morph across

anti_patterns: a still graphic for more than 2.2 s
hard cut between list items

how_by_engine.face-cam: alternate face and card at each item

entries.when: payoff / last image before the CTA
entries.do: Pull back or rise to a top-down or very wide frame so the whole consequence is visible (explosion, lone sign in the rain, the whole town upside down); hold 1.5-2.5 s; music resolves.

evidence.note: mushroom cloud payoff
lone neon sign in night rain
whole town walking upside down

anti_patterns: ending on a close-up with no consequence
cutting before the image can be read

how_by_engine.2d-flat: scale 100 to 80 % with the vignette opening
how_by_engine.board: all elements settle into a final tableau

entries.when: choosing an angle for any shot
entries.do: Low angle = power or threat; high angle = weakness or overview; dutch (6-12 degrees) = unease or chaos; top-down = map, gag or consequence; POV = immersion; over-the-shoulder = a conversation; eye-level = the default for explaining. Change the angle when the meaning changes, not for variety alone.

evidence.note: top-down desk laptop shot, bank/hospital low front shots
upside-down, ground-level and baby-POV angles for absurdity
driver POV inside the car for the psychology line

anti_patterns: same angle three shots in a row
dutch with no tension

how_by_engine.2d-flat: fake angle with perspective-skewed backdrop and a larger or smaller foreground figure
how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: move the camera; the sprite billboards
how_by_engine.face-cam: angle is the footage; use crop and rotation 2-4 degrees for dutch

entries.when: the audience must feel what a character feels (driving, riding, watching a screen)
entries.do: Place the camera inside the thing (car windscreen with wipers and dashboard, coaster seat, monitor reflection); 3-6 s; one sign, light or object in the vanishing point draws the eye.

evidence.note: rain windscreen, a lit tree in the distance as the lighthouse
top-down and rider views on the loop

anti_patterns: POV with no subject at the vanishing point

how_by_engine.2d-flat: flat windscreen frame layer over a scrolling road

entries.when: a phone call, TV news, CCTV, monitor or message carries the story
entries.do: Show the device filling 70-90 % of the frame, content playing inside it; the character's reaction is a separate cut within 1.5 s; sound: device speaker EQ on the voice (band-pass 400-3400 Hz).

evidence.note: phone call, red-map TV news, CCTV 9-monitor wall
TV on a pole with a skull

anti_patterns: device too small to read
voice not filtered

how_by_engine.2d-flat: frame layer + inner clip with masking

entries.when: deciding how often to cut in this style
entries.do: Use the style's cuts per 10 s and median shot length; vary adjacent shot lengths by at least 25 %; cut on the end of a phrase, on a beat or on a visual event; hold longer on shots that carry narration; never hold longer than the style's max hold without something changing inside.

evidence.note: medians measured over the 27 references, reference-library/dna27/INDEX.json

anti_patterns: metronome cutting (equal lengths)
cut mid-word

how_by_engine.board: count reveals inside the shot as cuts for pacing

entries.do: Something must move or change every 1.5 s: camera drift 1-2 %, a layer parallax, a blink, a breath, a counter tick, a particle. A frozen frame reads as a bug.

evidence.note: even the 72 s silent film keeps eyes darting and a slow push
eyes move, nothing else, and it holds

anti_patterns: drift in a single direction for 20 s

how_by_engine.board: ambient glow pulse + parallax of the grid

entries.when: choosing how to leave a shot
entries.do: Hard cut by default; blur-cut for a time jump or a swap between face and card; whip for a reveal; match-cut when two shots share a shape; dip to dark for a chapter end; no cross-dissolves in viral styles.

evidence.note: blur transition 0.3 s between cutaway and face
hard cuts with whoosh

anti_patterns: stock wipe or star transitions

entries.when: planning camera moves for any story short (all engines)
entries.do: Keep the camera moving about 75 percent of the time and drifting almost always (above 2 percent of frame width per second). Mix the moves like the measured reference: push-in 53 percent, pull-back 22 percent, tilt or crane 13 percent, pan, truck or arc 12 percent. About one distinct move every 2.2 s; median move 1.3 s; median hold between moves 0.4 s, and even a hold creeps in.

evidence.note: measured on three 65 s story shorts (Ricks Clips style) by the animated-shorts-kit: camera moving 73-83 percent, push-in 53 percent of moves

anti_patterns: a static camera for 4 s or more
linear moves or hard stops
a cut where a travelling move could carry the eye

entries.when: timing any camera move to the voice
entries.do: Ramp up in about 0.3 s, peak at about 40 percent of the move, settle more slowly; no linear moves. The move lands ON the narration noun or verb so the subject is reached as the word is spoken. Fast moves carry real motion blur.

evidence.note: velocity peak position 40-43 percent of each move, ease-in 0.4-0.6 and longer settle in all three measured shorts

anti_patterns: constant-speed dolly
the push arriving after the word is spoken

how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: drive dolly and fov with smootherstep keys; add a 3-6 frame motion blur on moves above 60 percent of frame width per second
how_by_engine.2d-flat: scale and translate the layer with a back-ease out; blur 2-3 px at peak

entries.when: two or more subjects or beats in the same place within about 4-5 s
entries.do: Use one continuous take that travels subject to subject (push on the speaker, pull-back plus arc or pan to the next) instead of cutting. Average shot 4.2 s (3.4-5.0). About one hard cut per video, placed on a mood switch or a punchline reaction.

evidence.note: one true hard cut per 65 s short; the other edits were 3-6 frame dissolves; examples show one camera visiting three subjects in 3 s

anti_patterns: a cut every 1.5 s
crowd or props popping in because staging changed between cuts

how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: keep staging continuous across a take (characters and props stay where they are), key the camera with cinema.js moves

entries.when: a change of location or time ("next day", "meanwhile", inside the jar)
entries.do: Edit with a 3-6 frame cross-dissolve (about 0.1-0.2 s); use a 6-frame white flash for a time jump or shock; use a whip or a foreground object passing the lens only to hide an unavoidable staging change.

evidence.note: 11-17 short cross-dissolves per 65 s, at location and time changes

anti_patterns: long slow cross-fades
a dissolve inside a continuous action

entries.when: writing the camera of any 3D shot (sprite-in-3d, 3d) that needs more than one move inside one shot
entries.do: Use movement.type "take" with keys [{t, framing, angle, subject, az, roll, distScale}] (t = fraction of the shot). The renderer solves each key as a pose and eases between them with the velocity peak at 40 percent of each leg plus a 1.2 percent creep-in, so the camera never stops. Put the main key at the emphasised word of the line; use distScale 1.65 on close-up and 1.3 on medium-close-up for 9:16 so a head fits; never extreme-close-up on a ball-head toon.

evidence.note: camera grammar: one camera visits several subjects per take; velocity peak 40 percent
our stills: extreme close-ups gave cap-only frames until distScale and cyScale were added

anti_patterns: extreme-close-up on a ball-head character in 9:16
low angle on a close lens (camera under the chin)

how_by_engine.sprite-in-3d: tools/lib/scene_planner.mjs emits the keys; cinema.js cameraAt type take solves them
